new_sources.title: BadScientist: Can a Research Agent Write Convincing but Unsound Papers that Fool LLM Reviewers?

candidate_mechanisms.description: A reviewer saying that it noticed an integrity concern is not enough. Integrity evidence must affect the decision mechanically or through a separately calibrated gate. Scientific review should verify provenance/execution artifacts where possible rather than relying on manuscript pattern recognition, and risk signals should be decision-coupled instead of appended as advisory text.
quantitative_evidence: Fabricated-but-polished papers with no real experiments achieved acceptance rates up to 82.0% under a three-model review panel calibrated on ICLR 2025 outcomes.
For one high-acceptance manipulation, calibrated acceptance was 67.0% and probability-consistent acceptance 82.0%, while panel-level integrity concern rate was only 39.5%.

Concern-acceptance conflict was common: conditional on a reviewer raising an integrity concern, acceptance-level scoring still occurred at rates ranging from 25.8% to 52.0% for o3 on the tested manipulations, with several 50%–100% cells for other reviewers on small flagged subsets.

Adding a mandatory integrity subtask (Review-with-Detection) raised panel-level concern rate 57.3%→86.0% but paradoxically raised calibrated acceptance 28.0%→44.0% and probability-consistent acceptance 37.0%→58.0%.

On a controlled 100-paper set (50 real ICLR 2025, 50 generated), ReD detector accuracy was 67% for o3 but 46% for o4-mini and 50% for GPT-4.1; detection-only accuracy was 57%, 45%, and 56% respectively, with large false-positive/false-negative tradeoffs.
candidate_mechanisms.evidence_scope: Presentation-manipulation attack without executable code or real data, no prompt injection/collusion, three reviewer models, standard single-pass paper-only review. The review system was intentionally not allowed to run experiments or inspect artifacts, so the failure does not measure provenance-aware or execution-aware reviewers. Acceptance calibration is ICLR 2025 specific.
candidate_mechanisms.decision_relevance: Very high for O evaluator design: a reviewer can explicitly notice a problem yet still produce a favorable scalar score. Therefore integrity/provenance failures should be separately typed and allowed to block or qualify downstream claims rather than being averaged into a generic quality score. This supports ScientistOne/EviGraph-style evidence binding and hard integrity fences over 'be more careful' reviewer prompting.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Explicit integrity-warning prompts increased stated concern detection but also increased acceptance in the tested review pipeline.
new_failure_evidence.scope: Three LLM reviewers on the paper-only BadScientist setup.
new_failure_evidence.implication: O should not infer that because an evaluator mentions a caveat, the caveat actually controls selection. Decision logic needs explicit typed gates/weights and behavioral tests.

new_failure_evidence.observation: The paper provides concentration/aggregation guarantees that reduce review-score variance, yet fabricated work is still frequently accepted. Mathematical aggregation reliability does not repair validity of the underlying reviewers.
new_failure_evidence.scope: The paper's three-reviewer aggregation and calibrated acceptance setup.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Distinguish precision/reliability of evaluator aggregation from validity against scientific truth; O evaluator quorums can become confidently wrong if all members share a blind spot.

new_failure_evidence.observation: Detection-only and review-plus-detection variants were near chance for several model configurations and showed severe sensitivity/specificity tradeoffs.
new_failure_evidence.scope: The controlled 100-paper detection set and three tested reviewer models.
new_failure_evidence.implication: Use artifact/provenance/execution-grounded checks or externally calibrated domain validators rather than generic self-reported fabrication detection when possible.

synthesis_with_prior_records.observation: Record 009 strengthens the pattern from records 004-008: independent-looking review layers are not sufficient by themselves. Hard formal/deterministic checks can guarantee specified properties; provenance-before-prose and evidence graphs constrain what may be claimed; immutable evaluator/data fences protect integrity surfaces; external/domain oracles ground inferential correctness; and reviewer panels must be calibrated for correlated errors. BadScientist adds a distinct action-gap: even a reviewer that notices integrity problems may fail to let that knowledge control the acceptance decision.
synthesis_with_prior_records.not_claimed: This does not show O's current evaluator has the same failure rate, nor that manuscript review should be a privileged O completion gate. It is evidence for testing whether recognized constraints actually control O's concrete downstream actions.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Do not treat the paper's recommended mandatory human oversight as a user-imposed O objective. The transferable evidence is the failure of paper-only LLM integrity review and the need for grounded/decision-coupled checks.
Do not generalize the 82% maximum acceptance rate to all scientific domains or richer review systems; the attack and reviewer access are narrowly specified.
Do not interpret higher integrity-warning rate as a successful mitigation when acceptance simultaneously rises; behavior/outcome control matters more than verbal acknowledgment.
Do not infer that adding more reviewer models fixes validity; record 008 independently shows strong correlated error and low effective independence in judge panels.
next_queries: Find scientist-agent review systems that let reviewers execute code or inspect immutable experiment artifacts, with controlled comparison against paper-only review.
Find quantitative interventions that mechanically couple integrity/provenance flags to selection while measuring false rejections and downstream scientific quality.
Find matched experiments testing whether cross-model reviewers plus artifact-grounded checks are complementary or redundant.
Find behavioral tests of context-to-action/constraint-to-action gaps in autonomous research agents: cases where a constraint is correctly verbalized but violated in subsequent action.
Continue evaluator covariance, transfer-applicability, and domain-oracle searches.

continuation.exact_resume_from: Continue after record 009. Priority: execution/artifact-aware reviewer ablations, decision-coupled integrity gates, cross-model plus grounded-check interaction, constraint-to-action behavioral tests, evaluator covariance, and memory applicability. Do not re-cover records 001-009 unless extracting new causal evidence, replication, or contradiction.
